tasks.short: Verify equipment amounts and quality before an expedition

steps.what: Read the expedition's approved equipment requirements
Count the actual equipment available for the expedition
Inspect equipment quality, serviceability and visible defects
Enter actual counts and condition findings on the existing kit checklist
Compare recorded usable amounts against the required equipment quantities
Check discrepancies and repair incomplete comparisons before deciding equipment readiness

tasks.design: Configure the existing {SPREADSHEET} kit checklist to reuse trip headings and calculate quantity differences from the guide's actual counts. Retain physical counting, serviceability inspection, discrepancy review and manual repair; the sheet does not certify equipment as safe.
tasks.previous_blocker: A packing checklist can mix repeat headings and numerical comparisons with physical safety checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas and a reusable kit template can handle repeated fields and exact count differences.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether worn equipment is safe for a particular trip.
tasks.human_edge: The guide physically inspects equipment and understands the consequences of a failure in the field.
tasks.altitude: Less checklist repetition and arithmetic; equipment readiness responsibility stays with the guide.

reach.learn: Equipment-specific inspection limits and shortage handling

evidence.claim: A native checklist template and formulas can reuse trip headings and compare captured quantities, while physical equipment inspection remains manual.

assumptions: The scenario uses the actual pre-departure kit checklist that the guide consults for readiness. No additional inspection register or report is introduced. This task ends at verification, without equipment purchases, supplier sends or a departure authorization transaction.

The organizer supplies the existing trip identifier, date, kit items and required quantities in equipment requirements. The guide reads them in s1, physically counts in s2, inspects in s3 and enters actual item identifiers, count, unusable count and observed defects in s4. Capture is retained, not supplied free by an inventory sensor.

The template removes two of ten entry hours by reusing trip headings and kit item rows. Eight remain for actual observations and missing-field repair. The separate nine comparison hours are only arithmetic on compatible items; all five review hours retain discrepancy meaning and failed-formula or unmatched-item repair after comparison.

Requirement selection and inspection standards remain existing work. Shares are unmeasured estimates. Ordinary saving is one fully retained hour without a self-approval gate; no machine safety judgment or automatically cleared equipment status is proposed.
unknowns: Is a per-trip kit checklist actually kept and used?
Which equipment items need incompatible units or individualized allocations?
research_questions: Can formulas preserve actual unusable-item counts without marking uninspected equipment serviceable?

already_counted.description: Observed count and condition entry plus discrepancy and failed-comparison repair

incremental.description: Maintain kit rows and test quantity formulas when equipment requirements change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 2 repeated-entry hours plus 9 arithmetic hours removed, less 1 upkeep gives 10. Conservative case: individualized kits require all nine comparison hours manually, while the two repeated trip-heading hours still disappear; less one upkeep leaves one.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach novices outdoor techniques and demonstrate equipment use

steps.what: Read the current instruction card and establish novice experience
Set up equipment and the safe practice area
Instruct novices in outdoor techniques and demonstrate correct equipment use
Supervise novice practice and correct unsafe technique immediately
Give individual feedback and decide whether to repeat supervised practice

tasks.design: Retain the existing {DOCS} instruction card and direct supervised practice. Native card access is already sufficient in this scenario; software does not remove physical demonstration, observation or corrective feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe technique depends on actual equipment handling and immediate correction.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is assumed to replace qualified field instruction.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a novice can perform a technique safely under changing conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The guide notices a dangerous movement and intervenes before it becomes an accident.

reach.task: Give technique feedback during supervised practice

evidence.claim: Physical demonstration and supervised novice practice require contextual observation and immediate intervention; a document template does not replace these acts.

assumptions: The task is the actual instruction session, including its real card reading and equipment setup. It does not establish routine new handouts, progress registers, certificates or written pupil assessments. None is added to create an administrative baseline. If a qualification scheme actually requires a written assessment, its real writing and release must be modeled for that different episode.

The activity lead supplies the current instruction card as existing unchanged work. The guide checks the relevant card in s1; native headings are already directly accessible. Known novice experience is verified through direct interaction, with no free transcript or capability score.

All five reading hours remain because they concern current technique and suitability, not browsing a long library. Setup, demonstrations, observation and spoken feedback all remain. Physical safety decisions are not automatic sends or record commits.
No change is deployed; incremental upkeep is explicitly zero. Shares are provisional task estimates, not measured instruction times.
unknowns: Does this instruction session carry an actual written qualification requirement?
Is the instruction card directly available?
research_questions: Does observing a real session identify an existing written assessment or repeated card search absent from this scenario?

already_counted.description: Current instruction-card reading and suitability check

incremental.description: No deployed system or additional upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 100 hours remain after separately checking actual card access and physical preparation. No routine written output is established, and existing direct card access leaves no template saving or new upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Remove limited kit-checklist repetition while keeping physical equipment safety and novice instruction with the guide.
reach: Coordinate equipment readiness with recreation workers
Exchange technique-feedback methods with exercise trainers
role.ambitious_version: A guide with less checklist arithmetic and unchanged responsibility for equipment condition and safe field instruction.
